name: Sulphur
mobility: IMMOBILE / poorly mobile (deficiency on YOUNG leaves first — looks like N but on new growth)

overview.whyImportant: Sulphur is the 4th major nutrient and the #1 hidden deficiency in Indian oilseeds and pulses. It builds sulphur-containing amino acids (cysteine, methionine), proteins, oils and the enzymes of N metabolism. A crop can look N-deficient but actually be S-starved — urea won't fix it.

plantFunctions.roleInsidePlant: Component of amino acids cysteine/methionine, proteins, coenzyme A, vitamins, and oil synthesis.
plantFunctions.rootDevelopment: Supports nodulation in legumes and root growth.
plantFunctions.vegetativeGrowth: Needed for protein-building; deficiency yellows new growth.
plantFunctions.fruitDevelopment: Drives OIL content in oilseeds and pungency in alliums/crucifers.
plantFunctions.proteinSynthesis: Essential — S-amino acids are the backbone of proteins.
plantFunctions.enzymeActivation: Part of key enzymes including those of N assimilation.
plantFunctions.chlorophyllFormation: Indirect but strong — deficiency causes chlorosis.
plantFunctions.yieldContribution: Major in oilseeds/pulses/crucifers — oil %, protein, and yield.

whyDeficiencyHappens.why: Sandy alkaline soils often low in S; leaching of sulphate.
Acid sandy soils low in organic S.
Low organic matter (main S source) and sulphate leaches.
Sulphate is mobile and leaches like nitrate.
Sulphate reduced to sulphide, unavailable/toxic in anaerobic soil.
Most soil S comes from organic matter mineralisation — low OM = low S.
High N without S limits protein synthesis; N:S ratio matters.
Shift from ammonium sulphate/SSP to urea/DAP removed the incidental S farmers used to add — the main modern cause.
Ignoring S entirely in oilseed/pulse nutrition — extremely common.

symptoms.note: S is poorly mobile — deficiency starts on YOUNG/upper leaves (unlike N which hits old leaves). Uniform pale-yellow young growth.
symptoms.early: Young/upper leaves pale-green to yellow, uniform (whole leaf, not interveinal).
symptoms.middle: General yellowing of newer leaves, stunted spindly growth, delayed maturity.
symptoms.severe: Whole plant pale-yellow, stunted, thin stems, poor pods/oil; older leaves may also yellow later.
symptoms.youngLeaves: First and worst: uniform pale-yellow (chlorosis of the whole young leaf).
symptoms.stem: Thin, short, woody; reddish tinge in some crops.
symptoms.fruit: Low oil content in oilseeds, poor pod fill.
symptoms.seed: Low oil %, reduced protein and seed quality.
symptoms.wholePlant: Pale-yellow especially at the top, stunted, late-maturing — the 'N-deficiency on the wrong (young) leaves' picture.

cropWiseSymptoms.symptoms: Young leaves pale-yellow, stunted, delayed — on sandy/leached soils.
Upper leaves uniformly pale-yellow, poor nodulation, low oil — S is critical for soybean.
Young-leaf yellowing, poor nodulation and low oil; responds strongly to gypsum.
Young leaves pale, stunted plants, poor growth.
Pale new leaves in low-S fertigation.
Young-leaf yellowing, whip-like thin leaves in severe cases (crucifers are high S-users).
Pale young leaves, reduced head size (high S demand crop).
Interveinal to uniform yellowing of YOUNGER leaves (vs N on older), stunting.
Pale young leaves on sandy soils.
Young-leaf yellowing, poor nodulation and pod fill.
Young-leaf yellowing, thin canes on S-poor soils.

howToFix.methodOfApplication: Broadcast + incorporate; the cheapest S source, bonus calcium
howToFix.precautions: Best value S for oilseeds/pulses; also improves sodic soils.

howToFix.methodOfApplication: Broadcast + incorporate; slow steady S release
howToFix.precautions: Apply well before peak demand (oxidation takes time).

howToFix.methodOfApplication: Broadcast/band; supplies P + S together — ideal for oilseeds/pulses
howToFix.precautions: Two nutrients in one; prefer over DAP where S is needed.

howToFix.methodOfApplication: Soil; supplies N + S; acidifying (good on alkaline soils)

methodOfApplication.broadcast: Gypsum/bentonite-S/SSP broadcast + incorporate as basal — the main S method.
methodOfApplication.foliarSpray: For quick relief, foliar sulphate via MgSO4 (1-2%); elemental S dust also used on some crops.
methodOfApplication.dripFertigation: Sulphate salts (MgSO4/SOP/ammonium sulphate soluble) via drip.
methodOfApplication.seedTreatment: Not applicable (Rhizobium seed treatment complements S in legumes).

toxicity.whatHappens: S toxicity is rare; excess elemental S sharply LOWERS soil pH; in waterlogged soil sulphate becomes toxic H2S/sulphide.
toxicity.plantToxicitySymptoms: Acidification stress; in rice, H2S root injury (blackened roots) in reduced soils.
toxicity.yieldLoss: Via acidity or sulphide root damage.
toxicity.correctionMethods: Avoid over-use of elemental S; improve drainage/aeration in rice to prevent sulphide; lime if over-acidified.

prevention: Include S in EVERY oilseed and pulse nutrition plan — assume deficiency on sandy/low-OM soils.
Use SSP instead of DAP where P and S are both needed.
Apply gypsum 80-120 kg/acre basal in oilseeds/pulses.
Use ammonium sulphate as part of N to add S.
Apply bentonite-S well ahead of peak demand (slow oxidation).
On sandy soils, expect leaching — apply S each season.
Diagnose by YOUNG-leaf yellowing (vs N on old leaves).
commonFarmerMistakes: Assuming urea will fix pale crop when the real problem is sulphur (young leaves yellow).
Switching fully to urea/DAP and dropping the S that SSP/ammonium sulphate used to provide.
Ignoring S in oilseeds/pulses — the biggest yield leak.
Confusing S deficiency (young leaves) with N deficiency (old leaves).
Applying bentonite-S too late (it needs time to oxidise).
Using DAP-only where SSP would add needed S.
Not applying S on sandy leached soils.
Ignoring organic matter that supplies S.
Over-applying elemental S and acidifying soil.
Applying sulphate to waterlogged rice (sulphide toxicity).
Skipping soil test for available S.
Wrong N:S ratio (too much N, no S).
Not repeating S on leaching-prone soils each season.
Believing NPK blends cover S (most don't).
Delaying S until symptoms are severe.
expertTips: Diagnose S by uniform YELLOWING of the YOUNGEST leaves (N does the oldest).
For oilseeds/pulses, budget 80-120 kg gypsum/acre as standard.
Prefer SSP over DAP wherever both P and S are needed.
Ammonium sulphate covers N + S and suits alkaline soils.
Apply bentonite-S well ahead of demand — it must oxidise to sulphate first.
Keep N:S near 10-12:1 for efficient protein synthesis.
Build organic matter as the base S reservoir.
On sandy soils, apply S every season — sulphate leaches like nitrate.
Gypsum doubles as a Ca source and sodic-soil amender.
MgSO4/SOP conveniently supply S with Mg/K.
S drives OIL % in oilseeds — don't skip it in mustard/soybean/groundnut.
Crucifers (cauliflower/cabbage) are high S-users — plan for it.
Avoid sulphate on waterlogged rice (H2S risk); improve aeration.
Confirm with soil test for available S where response is unclear.
Combine S with Rhizobium in legumes for max nodulation + protein.
Don't over-apply elemental S — it acidifies soil.
Use foliar sulphate (MgSO4) for quick top-up while soil S builds.
Watch the crop TOP (new growth) for early S signs.
Record S inputs — it's the nutrient most often forgotten.
Pair balanced N with S so N is actually converted to protein.

faq.q: Upar ki (nayi) patti pili ho rahi hai, N daalun?
faq.a: Nahi — nayi patti pili matlab SULPHUR ki kami (N ki kami purani patti par). Gypsum/SSP/ammonium sulphate dein.
S se oil % aur protein banta hai aur legume me nodulation sudharta hai — sabse chhupi kami yahi hai.
Gypsum (18% S + calcium), 80-120 kg/acre basal.
Jahan P + S dono chahiye (oilseed/pulse), SSP behtar — P ke saath sulphur bhi.
Demand se pehle (basal) — use oxidise hone me time lagta hai.

faq.q: N aur S deficiency me farak?
faq.a: N = neeche/purani patti pili; S = upar/nayi patti pili. Yahi sabse aasaan pehchaan.
Har season dein — sulphate nitrate ki tarah leach ho jata hai.
N + S dono; alkaline mitti me acidifying effect bhi accha.

faq.q: S ka asar kitne din me?
faq.a: Gypsum/SSP 2-3 hafte; foliar sulphate 7-10 din.

faq.q: NPK blend me S hota hai?
faq.a: Zyadatar me nahi — alag se S plan karein.
Oil % aur yield dono badhte hain — S mustard ke liye critical.
Lagbhag 10-12:1 — tabhi N protein me badalta hai.
Sulphate reduce hokar H2S ban sakta hai (jad kaali) — aeration/drainage rakhein.
Gobhi high S-user hai — plan me zaroor rakhein.
Mitti bahut acidic ho jati hai — seemit maatra.
MgSO4 1-2% (S + Mg) quick top-up ke liye.
Dono saath — max nodulation aur protein.
Crop ke TOP (nayi growth) par jaldi symptom dikhta hai.
Calcium bhi milta hai aur sodic mitti sudharti hai.
Nahi — nutrient disorder; uniform young-leaf yellowing, fungicide bekaar.
